messages.author: 9c510cde52a25986
messages.subject: cutoff_predictor(thresholds, fraction = 0.5)
parts:
Hi!
Can someone please explain what "fraction" specifies in cutoff_predictor(thresholds, fraction = 0.5)
The documentation states the "fraction of the data to seek the threshold" but I am still confused.
An example to help understand would be very helpful too!
Thanks!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] cutoff_predictor(thresholds, fraction = 0.5)
parts:
Hello,

This refers to the fraction of cutoff thresholds. If you line up the thresholds from smallest to largest, normally you would expect to find a cutoff point within the first 50% of these, but in the latter half, you might find some thresholds that are separated far apart, which would predict a cutoff at a very great genetic distance, which is not great for detecting multilocus lineages.


Hope that helps,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] cutoff_predictor(thresholds, fraction = 0.5)
parts:
The default should be sufficient, but the easiest way would be to plot the cutoffs using the filter_stats() function. More info here: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/filter_stats.html


Best,

Zhian
